text: Goa is a coastal destination known for beaches, festivals, Portuguese-era architecture, temples and churches. The Incredible India guide highlights both coastal and heritage experiences.
The Incredible India guide lists beaches including Baga, Calangute, Palolem and Agonda, and heritage sites including Basilica of Bom Jesus, Se Cathedral and Fort Aguada.
Goa's listed airports are Manohar International Airport (GOX) and Dabolim Airport (GOI). Goa Tourism also describes air, road and sea access to the state; check current schedules before travel.
The Incredible India guide describes Goan cuisine as influenced by Indian, Portuguese and Konkani traditions, and names fish curry rice, prawn balchao, xacuti, vindaloo and bebinca.
Goa Tourism Development Corporation lists bus and road connections and passenger cruise services. Confirm routes, operators and schedules with current providers.
Goa Police advises visitors to respect local customs and traditions and observe decorum in dress at religious places. It also advises following lifeguard directions in designated bathing areas.
Goa Police warns tourists to beware of tout inducements and to deal with authorized persons or agents. The department also advises against buying tickets through strangers or unauthorized agents.
Goa Police advises visitors not to leave belongings unattended, not to enter the sea at night especially after drinking, and to follow lifeguard instructions in designated bathing zones.

Goa Tourism describes local private buses as a wide-network, lower-cost option and says a ticket costs approx INR 10 for 2-3 km; check the route board and verify current fares. GTDC lists motorcycle taxis (pilots), ferries on named river crossings, Goa Miles app cabs and rentals. Its published approximate starting figures include Rs 50 for motorcycle taxis and rental ranges by bike type; confirm current terms locally.
